decisions.title: Adopt Microservices Architecture
decisions.decision: Use Microservices as the primary architecture style.
decisions.context: The banking platform requires independent scalability, fault isolation, high availability and independent service deployment.
decisions.rationale: Microservices provide independent deployment and scaling while improving fault isolation between major banking capabilities.
rejected_alternative_reasons: Layered Architecture provides limited independent scalability.
Modular Monolith simplifies deployment but provides weaker service-level isolation.
Event-Driven Architecture is useful for asynchronous processing but was not selected as the primary architecture style.
consequences: The system must manage communication between independent services.
Deployment and monitoring infrastructure becomes more complex.
trade_offs: Higher operational complexity in exchange for improved scalability and service independence.

decisions.title: Use PostgreSQL for Transaction Data
decisions.decision: Use PostgreSQL as the main database for financial transaction records.
decisions.context: Financial transactions require structured relationships, consistency and reliable transaction handling.
decisions.rationale: PostgreSQL provides relational modelling and ACID transaction guarantees suitable for financial transaction records.
rejected_alternative_reasons: MongoDB was not selected because the primary transaction records require stronger relational consistency.
Cassandra was not selected because the use case prioritises transaction consistency over large-scale distributed write throughput.
risks: Horizontal scaling may require additional configuration.
consequences: Transactional data will follow relational schemas.
trade_offs: Stronger consistency is prioritised over schema flexibility.

decisions.title: Use REST APIs for Client Communication
decisions.decision: Expose banking functionality to web and mobile clients through REST APIs.
decisions.context: The system requires interoperable communication between web clients, mobile clients and backend services.
decisions.rationale: REST provides standard HTTP-based communication that is widely supported by client platforms.
rejected_alternative_reasons: GraphQL introduces additional query-layer complexity that is not required for the initial design.
gRPC has weaker direct browser compatibility for the intended client-facing APIs.
risks: Multiple requests may be required for complex client workflows.
consequences: Client-facing endpoints must follow consistent REST conventions.
trade_offs: Simplicity and compatibility are prioritised over specialised RPC performance.

decisions.title: Require Token-Based Authentication
decisions.decision: Protected banking APIs must use token-based authentication and authorization.
decisions.context: Banking operations process sensitive user and financial information and therefore require controlled access.
decisions.rationale: Token-based authentication supports stateless API security and can be combined with role-based authorization.
rejected_alternative_reasons: Server-side sessions introduce additional shared session-state requirements across independently deployed services.
risks: Token expiration and revocation must be handled securely.
consequences: Protected endpoints must validate authentication tokens.
trade_offs: Stateless authentication reduces session-state requirements but introduces token lifecycle management.
